texts.orig: As long as S is strongly E ∗ -unitary, the resulting algebra L R ( S, ϕ ) is isomorphic irrespective of the chosen group G and map ϕ : S × → G , hence we unambiguously write L R ( S ) whenever we don't need to keep a specific grading in mind. For two strongly E ∗ -unitary inverse semigroups S 1 and S 2 , we say that S 1 ⊆ c S 2 if S 1 ⊆ S 2 and E 1 ⊆ E 2 preserves finite covers. If S 1 ⊆ c S 2 , then for any group G and grading ϕ : S × 2 → G on S 2 there is an induced grading ϕ | S × 1 on S 1 . Furthermore, the induced partial actions from these gradings satisfy ( T c ( E 1 ) , Φ 1 ) ⊆ ( T c ( E 2 ) , Φ 2 ) and hence L R ( S 1 ) ⊆ L R ( S 2 ).

texts.orig: When we refer to Morita equivalence in this paper, we are referring to the notion of Morita equivalence in rings with local units first developed by Abrams in [4] and further explored by Anh and Marki in [24]. We will denote Morita equivalent rings with local units R and S as R ∼ M S .
texts.text: When we refer to Morita equivalence in this paper, we are referring to the notion of Morita equivalence in rings with local units first developed by Abrams in [4] and further explored by Anh and Marki in [24]. We will denote Morita equivalent rings with local units R and S as R ∼ M S .

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In this section, we present a technique to prove that a subring S ⊆ R of a ring with local units is Morita equivalent. We will later apply this to the partial skew group rings and derive various conditions to make the rings Morita equivalent. Most of this section is a generalization of the ideas presented in [3] and [10] to prove a desingularization result for graph and ultragraph algebras respectively.

This lets our results apply to all rings with local units instead of just rings with σ -units, which will be useful later when we apply our results to objects that aren't necessarily countable.
